subject: ILCE-6400 updater crypto and receiver boundary

updater_mode_receiver.reason: The located command 0x40 handler writes to a 5 MiB accessory staging area and extracts ACCYFIRM.BIN; that cannot account for the 304833808-byte system FDAT resent after updater-mode reconnect.

observations.source: Signed Windows updater engine decompilation and pmca protocol source
observations.claim: The guard transfer starts with a zero-payload handshake and can terminate successfully after the first negotiated data chunk; the updater-mode recursion seeks back to the saved FDAT start before the complete command 0x40 transfer.
The normal-runtime guard decrypts only the first 512 bytes for model, region, and version fields, and its located full-write path stages an accessory image named ACCYFIRM.BIN in a 5 MiB tmpfs.

The located Dec_Scramble path processes 1024-byte frames with AES-128 ECB and exposes no CBC implementation, while the validated decoded layout is a 512-byte header, 143360-byte updater image, and 303498240-byte firmware archive.

observations.source: historical generation-four decryptor and alpha 6400 size arithmetic
observations.claim: The historical decryptor treats the final 272 bytes as a 16-byte IV followed by an ignored 256-byte suffix; subtracting that trailer leaves a 1024-byte-aligned ciphertext region.

inferences.source: Valid split ECB/CBC reconstruction combined with crypter ECB-only implementation
inferences.claim: A CBC transformation probably occurs in the updater-mode ingress path before crypter.elf, but its implementation, caller, and key origin have not been located.

inferences.source: Fixed 256-byte outer suffix and signed-generation documentation
inferences.claim: The outer suffix is a plausible authenticity object, but no verifier, signed range, trust anchor, or failure mapping has been proven.

unresolved.claim: The system receiver that accepts the full command 0x40 FDAT after re-enumeration remains unlocated.
No proven call chain connects the registered AES or UDRT secure application to the firmware CBC stage or to authenticity verification.
The semantic role and verification algorithm for the final 256 bytes remain unknown.

conclusion: The two-stage transport, normal-runtime header guard, accessory-only UFP write path, ECB crypter, decoded layout, and CRC layers are mapped. The separate system receiver, pre-crypter CBC implementation, outer-suffix verifier, and any SA invocation remain unresolved, so no bypass or installable model-mismatched image has been established.
